{"command": "cat > /workspace/create_figure.py <<'PY'
import textwrap
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

names = [
    'Department of Transportation and Infrastructure',
    'Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care',
    'Office of the Auditor General',
    'Department of Fisheries and Oceans',
    'Ministry of Education and Child Care',
    'Agency for Environmental Protection',
    'Department of Finance and Treasury Board',
    'Office of Indigenous Relations',
    'Ministry of Labour and Workforce Development',
    'Department of Agriculture and Agri-Food',
    'Office of the Chief Information Officer',
    'Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs',
    'Department of Justice and Public Safety',
    'Agency for Statistics and Data Services',
    'Ministry of Energy, Mines and Low Carbon Innovation',
    'Department of Tourism, Arts and Culture',
    'Office of the Ombudsperson',
    'Ministry of Forests and Range Management',
    'Department of Veterans Affairs',
    'Agency for Emergency Management',
    'Ministry of Post-Secondary Education and Skills',
    'Department of Public Works and Procurement',
    'Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner',
    "Ministry of Citizens' Services",
    'Department of Trade and Investment',
    'Agency for Water Stewardship',
    'Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction',
    'Department of Northern Affairs',
    'Office of the Seniors Advocate',
    'Ministry of Mental Health and Addictions',
]
values = [114, 240, 742, 427, 398, 101, 631, 585, 246, 769,
          198, 851, 22, 328, 763, 118, 162, 398, 701, 584,
          181, 254, 283, 635, 725, 885, 620, 390, 278, 475]

# Wrapping keeps the complete names readable while allowing the mandated rotation.
def wrap_name(name):
    return '\n'.join(textwrap.wrap(name, width=14, break_long_words=False,
                                  break_on_hyphens=False))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6), dpi=100)
# Reserve a compact chart area and ample, intentional space for the five label rows.
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.075, right=0.99, top=0.94, bottom=0.08)
ax.set_position([0.075, 0.54, 0.915, 0.39])
ax.bar(range(len(names)), values, color='#2a9d8f', width=0.8)
ax.set_ylim(0, 900)
ax.set_ylabel('IT budget (thousand $)')
ax.set_title('IT budget by department')
ax.set_xticks(range(len(names)))
ax.set_xticklabels([wrap_name(n) for n in names], rotation=60, ha='right', fontsize=8)

# Put six labels per row. They remain the actual x tick labels and align with bars.
# The separated rows prevent the long, rotated names from touching one another.
for i, label in enumerate(ax.get_xticklabels()):
    row = i // 6
    label.set_y(-0.035 - row * 0.185)
    label.set_clip_on(False)

fig.savefig('/workspace/figure.png', dpi=100)
plt.close(fig)
PY
cd /workspace && python create_figure.py
file /workspace/figure.png
python - <<'PY'

print('size:', im.size, 'mode:', im.mode)
PY"}
